**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ ۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدٌ﴾
And Musa said to them: Remember when your Lord proclaimed firmly: If you thank Him for His blessings, He will surely give you more of His bounty; and if you deny Allah's blessing, He will surely punish you with a severe punishment.

﴿وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ إِن تَكْفُرُوا أَنتُمْ وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾
And he said to them: If you disbelieve in Allah, you and all the people of the earth, you will not harm Allah in the least; for Allah is Free of need of His creation, deserving of all praise and commendation, praised in every situation.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Amir looked at his shoot and said, "This won't feed anyone," and Nabil said, "Alhamdulillah." What did each of them do with his shoot after what he said?
2. Nabil's thankfulness was not just a word he said with his tongue. With what action did he give thanks? (Thankfulness is praising Allah with the tongue, and taking good care of the blessing and using it in what pleases Him.)
3. How did Allah give Nabil more? And what did Nabil do when his brother came back with very little left in his hands?

**This week's exercise**
Plant a seed or a small seedling in a pot together. Your child takes charge of watering it every morning this week and says by it, "Alhamdulillah." At the end of the week, talk together about another blessing they have, which they can give thanks for by taking care of it, just as Nabil gave thanks for his shoot.
